records.name: Philadelphia Unemployment Project Jobs Club
records.summary: A Zoom job search group run by the Philadelphia Unemployment Project. Members share how their applications are going, and staff give short lessons on resumes, interviews and salary talks.
records.what_you_do: Share updates on your job applications, join the short staff trainings, and ask for a resume review or a practice interview.

schedule.text: Every other Thursday at 2 pm, on Zoom

first_step.how: The page gives no sign-up step for the club itself. Ask the Philadelphia Unemployment Project how to join before the first session.
first_step.basis: The club page does not say how to sign up, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The only dated item on the page is the 2021 start of the club, and the schedule itself is undated. Status left as unknown rather than guessing. The phone and email on the page are for unemployment benefit questions, so they are not listed as club contacts.

records.name: PA CareerLink Philadelphia
records.summary: The city's public job center network, funded through federal and state workforce programs. It offers free help with resumes, interviews and job searches, plus workshops and hiring events at centers and libraries.
records.what_you_do: Book a career appointment, attend a free workshop, or come to a hiring event and meet employers.

schedule.text: Workshops and hiring events through October 2026, held at centers and libraries. Sign up through the events calendar.

locations.label: North and Northwest centers, Suburban Station, West and South Philadelphia, and several Free Library branches

cost.text: Services and job search site are free. Awareness Day is free and open to all.

first_step.how: Call 1-833-750-5627, use the contact page to book an appointment, or register for an event on the events calendar.
first_step.basis: Open to the public at no cost, with a phone line and online booking.

records.notes: A public workforce service rather than a club. Hours of the general centers are not published, only event times. Listed events include an October 14, 2026 job and resource fair at Community College of Philadelphia (free registration). The October 22 wellness fair was taken from a Facebook post and is not recorded here.

records.name: Great Careers Network (Philadelphia Area Great Careers Group)
records.summary: A nonprofit career support group for job seekers in the Philadelphia area. It holds expert panels, skill workshops and peer meetups, and publishes free career resources.
records.what_you_do: Attend expert talks and working sessions, join peer meetups where members share advice, or read the free newsletter.

locations.label: Main office
locations.address: 53 Darby Road, Suite F, Paoli, PA 19301

cost.text: Event prices and membership cost are not stated on the homepage

first_step.how: Subscribe to the free newsletter, or sign up for membership at the membership page, then pick an event from the calendar.
first_step.basis: Free newsletter and membership sign-up are listed publicly, but event prices and the peer meetup format are not described.

records.notes: The office is in Paoli (Chester County), so in_city is false. The homepage links to an events calendar but lists no dated events, so the status is probably_active rather than active. The group also lists a Meetup page (meetup.com/philadelphia-area-great-careers-group/), which was not fetched. The redirect from greatcareersphl.org to greatcareers.org was followed.

records.name: Panorama Toastmasters
records.summary: A Philadelphia Toastmasters club that meets in person to practice public speaking and leadership. Guests can visit for free, as often as they like, before deciding to join.
records.what_you_do: Practice short speeches and impromptu talks, take on meeting roles, and get feedback from other members.

schedule.text: 1st and 3rd Wednesdays, 7:00 to 8:45 pm, and 2nd Saturdays, 1:00 to 2:45 pm. Meetings confirmed through December 2026.

locations.label: Thomas F. Donatucci, Sr. Library (Saturday meetings)

cost.text: Guests free. Dues about $15 a month, billed every six months, plus a one-time $40 fee for new members.

first_step.how: Come to a meeting as a guest, or contact the club first using the Contact section of its site.
first_step.basis: Guests are explicitly welcome, visit free, and can attend as often as they like before joining.

records.notes: The site says a new board took office July 1, 2026, that meetings have been in person since July 2023, and that the club is celebrating 30 years. The club has been meeting in person since 2023 at the two venues listed.

records.name: Philadelphia's First Toastmasters Club (Club 541)
records.summary: A Toastmasters club that meets online on Thursday evenings to practice speaking and leading meetings. Guests are always welcome to visit a meeting first.
records.what_you_do: Give short speeches, join impromptu speaking rounds, and take on meeting roles on Zoom.

schedule.text: Thursday evenings on Zoom, about 7 to 9 pm. Some upcoming meetings are listed at 6:45 pm. Upcoming dates include September 3 and October 15, 2026.

first_step.how: Join a Thursday meeting on Zoom using the link on the club site, or use the Contact page to plan a first visit.
first_step.basis: The club says guests are always welcome and invites visitors to attend an upcoming meeting.

records.notes: Meets only on Zoom, so there is no street address. The Zoom meeting ID and passcode on the site were deliberately not copied here. Cost is not stated on the site. The site shows both EDT and EST labels, so check the time before joining.

records.name: University City Toastmasters
records.summary: A Toastmasters club based in University City that welcomes students, graduates and working professionals who want to practice public speaking.
records.what_you_do: Practice speaking and leadership with other members once meetings are scheduled.

locations.label: University City, Philadelphia (meeting place not published)

first_step.how: Email the club at tm.universitycity@gmail.com, or use the Plan your first visit link on the club's Contact page.
first_step.basis: Guests are welcome, but no meeting dates, times or place are published yet, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The page says Schedule coming soon and No upcoming meetings have been published yet. The newest club item is a 2026 convention banner, which is not a club event. The site says the club is moving to universitycitytoastmasters.com, but that site refused the connection when checked, so it is unverified. Club number 1304762.

records.name: Northeast Philly Toastmasters Club (Club 1134526)
records.summary: A Toastmasters club with a Northeast Philadelphia name that meets online. Guests are welcome at any skill level and attend free after an RSVP.
records.what_you_do: Join an online meeting to try speaking, answer impromptu questions, or just watch and say what brought you.

first_step.how: RSVP on the club's Meetup page to get the Zoom link.
first_step.basis: The club says guests are welcome regardless of skill or confidence, and explains how to attend.

records.notes: The site says Schedule coming soon and no upcoming meetings are published, so the meeting day and time are unknown. The site footer shows a visitor counter starting in August 2025, which is not treated as proof the club is active. Meetup was not fetched, because Meetup is a lead-only platform. A search snippet said the Meetup page shows the club on hold, but that was not checked, so it is not relied on here.

records.name: Startup Grind Philadelphia
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of a worldwide startup community. Founders can join a membership to get networking, mentorship and office hours.
records.what_you_do: Apply for membership, then take part in chapter events, office hours and mentorship.

cost.text: The site describes membership as free access to events and mentorship, but some events cost money and prices are not listed.

first_step.how: Apply for a Startup membership at the link on the chapter page.
first_step.basis: Membership needs an application before you can see the chapter's events and mentors.

records.notes: The chapter page lists about 6,084 members and only past events, with no Philadelphia venue or dated event. The only address on the page is the corporate office in Palo Alto, California, so it is not recorded. Status is unknown rather than active.

records.name: Philly Tech Entrepreneurs
records.summary: A free Philadelphia community for tech founders, developers and designers, joined through a Slack group and Meetup. It has had in-person meetups and a podcast.
records.what_you_do: Introduce yourself in the Slack group, follow Meetup events, and attend a meetup.

cost.text: Joining is free. Some events have a ticket of about $10, listed in each event.

first_step.how: Join the Slack community and introduce yourself, then join the Meetup group and attend an event.
first_step.basis: Anyone can join the Slack group and Meetup, but the site lists no current events to attend.

records.notes: The newest dated item on the site is labeled PTE Meetups 2023, and no upcoming events are listed, so status is dormant. Member counts on the site disagree with each other (515 and 350 on Slack, 1,030 and 850 on Meetup). The Slack invite link is not recorded because invite links expire.

records.name: Compass Pro Bono (Philadelphia)
records.summary: Connects Philadelphia nonprofits with business professionals. Volunteers can take on short consulting projects or join a nonprofit's board after receiving board training.
records.what_you_do: Take on a consulting project for a nonprofit, guide a nonprofit leader for eight weeks, or serve on a board after training.

first_step.how: Create an account on the Compass site and apply through the volunteer opportunities page.
first_step.basis: Volunteers must apply and be matched, and the site does not say what the application involves.

records.notes: The page lists an On Track 4 and 8 month cohort for Fall but gives no year. Volunteer eligibility and cost are not stated. The only address published is the national office in Washington, DC, so no Philadelphia office is recorded. The managing director's name and email are on the page and were left out.

records.name: Key Skills Hub (The Philadelphia Foundation)
records.summary: An online matching tool where professionals volunteer their skills for local nonprofits. Typical projects include marketing plans, websites and graphic design.
records.what_you_do: Create a skills profile, look at nonprofit projects, and agree to a match with an organization.

cost.text: Free for nonprofits. The site does not state a volunteer cost.

first_step.how: Use the Volunteer link on the Key Skills Hub page to create a skills profile.
first_step.basis: Professionals at any career stage can sign up, and the site describes a mutual match before any work starts.

records.notes: The site lists 120 or more pre-scoped projects. The page footer shows a 2026 copyright, which is not treated as evidence. Two demo events appear with no dates. A search summary said the pages look about three years old, but that was not confirmed on the page itself.

records.name: Board Prep (Young Involved Philadelphia)
records.summary: A fall course for young professionals who want to learn nonprofit board service. It covers governance, fundraising and finance, and ends with a meeting with Philadelphia nonprofits looking for board members.
records.what_you_do: Attend the course sessions, hear from current board members, and connect with nonprofits seeking candidates at the graduation.

schedule.text: Fall session September 16 to November 11, 2026. Graduation November 11, 2026, 6 to 8 pm.

cost.text: Tuition applies. The amount is not stated on the page, and donations help cover it.

first_step.how: Fill in the Fall 2026 Board Prep application form linked on the page, or email boardprep@yiphilly.org to confirm it is still open.
first_step.basis: An application is needed, and the page gives two conflicting statuses for the fall application.

records.notes: One notice on the page says the Fall 2026 application is closed, and another says rolling admission runs until September 1. Confirm before telling anyone to apply. Minimum age is 21 because in-person events include alcohol. The site gives no weekly hours or session count.

records.name: Nonprofit Collaborative (LEADERSHIP Philadelphia)
records.summary: Connects LEADERSHIP Philadelphia alumni and Fellows with regional nonprofits that need board members. It offers introductions, short volunteer projects and one-time board observations.
records.what_you_do: Alumni and Fellows can observe a board, join a short Pay It Forward project, or be introduced to a nonprofit that is recruiting.

cost.text: Nonprofits pay a $250 yearly membership fee. No fee is listed for alumni or Fellows who volunteer.

first_step.how: LEADERSHIP Philadelphia alumni and Fellows complete the online form linked on the page. Nonprofits submit the application and pay the fee.
first_step.basis: Only alumni and Fellows can take part, and the way in is an online form.

records.notes: The newest dated notice is the 2025 enrollment window, which closed October 31, 2025. The 2026 dates were not posted on the page. The payment link on the page points to a domain that is not LEADERSHIP Philadelphia's, so it was not recorded. Confirm payment by phone before paying.

records.name: Business On Board
records.summary: A five week course that trains business and nonprofit professionals for board service, then matches some of them with arts and culture nonprofits. Fees apply.
records.what_you_do: Complete the course sessions and weekly reading, then optionally observe a board that is recruiting.

locations.label: The Nonprofit Center at La Salle University

schedule.text: Five week course, about 45 to 60 minutes a week of pre and post work, plus the sessions. The 2024 season is closed and no later dates are listed.

cost.text: From $500 to $3,000, depending on who pays and whether the observership is included. A 15 percent discount applies to several people from one organization.

first_step.how: Call (215) 951-1701 or use the contact page to ask whether a new cycle is open.
first_step.basis: Paid course that needs a sign-up, and the page says the latest season is closed.

records.notes: The page says The 2024 Business on Board season is closed and lists no 2025 or 2026 dates. The program page also says it moved to The Nonprofit Center at La Salle University, and the new site was not checked. Check whether a new cycle has opened before listing it as current.

records.name: OIC Philadelphia Financial Literacy Classes
records.summary: A job training nonprofit that teaches budgeting, banking, credit and saving alongside its job and adult education classes. One-on-one money coaching is also offered.
records.what_you_do: Build a working budget, set up a simple savings plan, check your credit report, and make a personal money plan.

locations.label: Job training programs at N Broad and Thompson streets

cost.text: The page says many programs like this are free or low cost, and advises confirming the cost with OIC.

first_step.how: Call (215) 236-7700 or send an inquiry through the OIC contact page.
first_step.basis: Open to the public with a phone line and inquiry form, though eligibility and class dates are not published.

records.notes: The source is an April 2026 article on the OIC site, not a class calendar. No schedule, eligibility or full street address is published. The email address on the page is obscured, so it was not recorded. Ask OIC which classes are open before the first visit.

records.name: P.O.W.E.R. Construction Pre-Apprenticeship (Trades for a Difference)
records.summary: A free seven week construction pre-apprenticeship for Philadelphia Housing Authority residents and Section 8 voucher holders. It includes safety certificates, a $500 gift and a route into apprenticeship.
records.what_you_do: Learn construction basics, earn safety and OSHA certificates, and choose carpentry, plumbing or electrical work.

schedule.text: Seven week program. Daily times and cohort start dates are not published.

cost.text: Free vocational training, with a $500 gift, paid lunch and other incentives listed.

first_step.how: Use the Register now link on the program page.
first_step.basis: Needs an application and proof of residency or voucher, and cohort dates are not listed.

records.notes: Eligibility is strict: PHA resident or Section 8 voucher holder, 18 or older, with a high school diploma or GED. The page lists no cohort dates or year. Also run in partnership with Associated Builders and Contractors.

records.name: WINC Tradeswomen Readiness Program
records.summary: A Philadelphia pre-apprenticeship for women who want higher paying skilled trade careers. It also helps build the math and personal skills needed to qualify.
records.what_you_do: Build math and job skills, learn about the trades, and get ready to apply for apprenticeships.

first_step.how: Use the Learn More and Apply link on the WINC page, which goes to the program's apply page.
first_step.basis: Needs an application, and eligibility and start dates are not stated on the page.

records.notes: Cost, eligibility, schedule and dates are not stated on the page. The phone number is the PhilaWorks administrative office, not a program line. Women Build PA runs the application page.

records.name: Philadelphia Association for Financial Professionals (PAFP)
records.summary: A professional association for treasury, finance and accounting workers in the Philadelphia area. It holds monthly educational events and a yearly conference.
records.what_you_do: Attend a monthly lunch and learn or conference, network with finance professionals, or join as a member.

schedule.text: Monthly educational events. Next listed: a virtual lunch and learn on October 22, 2026, noon to 1 pm.

cost.text: Event and membership prices are not listed on the page.

first_step.how: Use the Register for a Monthly Meeting link, or the online membership application.
first_step.basis: Events have public registration links and membership is open to students and individuals.

records.notes: The office is in Conshohocken (Montgomery County), and the association serves the Delaware Valley, so in_city is false. The email address on the page is obscured and was not recorded.

records.name: EAPA Greater Philadelphia Chapter
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of a national group for employee assistance professionals. It holds membership meetings and helps members and students with the costs of training.
records.what_you_do: Attend chapter membership meetings, study for the CEAP exam, and meet others who work in employee assistance.

cost.text: Meeting costs are not stated. The CEAP study guide costs $39.95 for members and $49.95 for non-members.

first_step.how: Email the chapter at philaeapa@gmail.com to ask how to attend a membership meeting.
first_step.basis: The site is written for members, and how non-members can attend is not stated.

records.notes: The one listed upcoming event is an October Membership Meeting on October 13, 2026. The venue and the regular meeting schedule are not stated on the page.

records.name: PSPE Philadelphia Chapter
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of the state engineers society. It runs monthly talks, site tours and continuing education courses, plus youth STEM and MathCounts programs.
records.what_you_do: Attend a monthly talk or tour, take a continuing education course, or view the free presentation recordings.

schedule.text: Monthly meetings, tours and courses. Listed dates run from September 2026 through May 2027. The page does not give a regular meeting day.

cost.text: Online professional development courses are $5 per PDH. The Engineers' Week banquet was $70. Separate chapter meeting fees are not stated.

first_step.how: Look at the programs on the chapter site and the membership page, then attend a listed event or course.
first_step.basis: The site says courses are offered to members and non-members, and recordings are free to view.

records.notes: Mailing address is c/o Temple University Civil Engineering, which is not a meeting place. The chapter's phone number on the page is partly letters and was not recorded. The page is inconsistent about the October 15 event, which is listed as both a tour and a talk.

records.name: Philly SHRM
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of the national human resources association. It runs events, webcasts, a job board and study groups for HR certification exams.
records.what_you_do: Attend a member meet up or webcast, join an exam prep study group, or use the job board.

schedule.text: Events in October 2026 include a member meet up on October 21 and a webcast on October 26. The symposium date is coming soon.

cost.text: Event prices are not listed. The site says members get big discounts on events.

first_step.how: Visit the membership page at phillyshrm.org/membership/ or use the Contact Us form.
first_step.basis: Public events and a membership page are listed, but non-member event access is not explained.

records.notes: The site gives no phone, email or street address, only a contact form. The meeting schedule is not listed. The homepage has a members login link.

records.name: FPA Philadelphia Tri-State Area
records.summary: The Philadelphia tri-state chapter of the Financial Planning Association. It offers education, networking and a six month mentorship program that pairs newer planners with experienced ones.
records.what_you_do: Attend education events and networking, or join the mentorship program if you are a newer planner.

schedule.text: Single events rather than a set meeting schedule. Upcoming: October 14, 2026 virtual event; December 10, 2026 holiday party.

cost.text: Member and non-member prices are not listed.

first_step.how: Register for an event through the linked registration form, or contact the chapter executive.
first_step.basis: Events have public registration links, and a mentorship program is offered for newer planners.

records.notes: The chapter has about 500 members. Its 2026 mentorship kickoff was February 26, 2026, and the program is likely closed to new entrants this year. The 2027 Northeast Symposium is in New York, so it is not a Philadelphia event.

records.name: AFP Greater Philadelphia Chapter
records.summary: The Greater Philadelphia chapter of the fundraising professionals association. It holds coffee talks, workshops and a yearly National Philanthropy Day event.
records.what_you_do: Attend a coffee conversation, join a virtual fundraising workshop, or go to the yearly philanthropy event.

locations.label: Coffee conversations in suburban offices (Glenmede and RSM)
Evening event at The Logan Hotel

schedule.text: Upcoming: October 15, October 19 (virtual), October 29, November 12 and November 19, 2026.

cost.text: Member and non-member prices are not listed on the page.

first_step.how: Use the Register Now link on any listed event, or the chapter contact form.
first_step.basis: Events list public registration links, but the page does not say how non-members attend.

records.notes: The chapter's mailing address is in Leesburg, Virginia, and it is listed as AFP Philadelphia on the page. The Philadelphia venues are the ones recorded. The phone number is the chapter's listed line.

records.name: Career Solutions Job Club
records.summary: A job club that meets in St. Cloud, Minnesota.

locations.label: St. Cloud, Minnesota
locations.address: 1542 Northway Dr, Door 2, St. Cloud, MN 56303

records.notes: Listed in a Philadelphia job club search, but the address and 320 area code point to Minnesota. Not a Philadelphia group.

records.name: The Master's Apprentice
records.summary: A faith-based pre-apprenticeship program based in Englewood, Colorado.
records.notes: Found in a Philadelphia trades search, but the program is run from Colorado and the page lists no Philadelphia site.

leads_only.name: Philadelphia Job Seekers
leads_only.note: Meetup only. Monthly informal happy hour meetups for job seekers. Not checked beyond a search summary.

leads_only.name: Philadelphia Startup CoFounders
leads_only.note: Meetup only. Free founder events and a Startup Oasis format. Not checked.

leads_only.name: Philadelphia Startup Founder 101
leads_only.note: Meetup only. Free founder learning events. Not checked.

leads_only.name: StartupCouncil.org Philly Tech Entrepreneurs and Investors
leads_only.note: Meetup only. Online founder office hours. Not checked.

leads_only.name: Philadelphia Business Networking Group (PhillyBNG)
leads_only.note: Meetup only. Free membership and business networking events. Not checked.

leads_only.name: Philadelphia Area Toastmasters Clubs
leads_only.note: Meetup only. Directory-style group that may list other Philadelphia Toastmasters clubs. Not checked.

blocked.note: SCORE Greater Philadelphia page returned HTTP 403, so its free mentoring and workshop details were not recorded. It may be worth a future check by a human.
Connection refused when fetched. The University City Toastmasters site says it is the new home, but it could not be checked.

notes: Searches: all 10 used (list pages first, then gaps). Fetches: 33. Budget was not exhausted by fetches. Dropped on purpose (not written as records): JEVS Career Solutions for 55+ (Philadelphia, free, but one to one counseling rather than a group; belongs in a services lane); Veterans Multi-Service Center Women Veterans Program (drop-in community space with no job group named); The Veterans Group (broad veterans support, no jobs program named); SHRM and other chapters without a fetchable schedule were kept as records with low detail. Not yet checked: Haverford and Blue Bell Toastmasters (outside the city); Toasters Digest, Dungeons and Toast, and Thrivers and Survivors (online Toastmasters-linked clubs, not Philadelphia specific, no URLs fetched); 40Plus (no current Philadelphia chapter confirmed). Budget note: Business On Board and Trades for a Difference both show dated gaps, and several fee amounts are not stated on the pages, so cost levels are unknown where the page did not say. Search summaries were not used as facts unless a fetched page confirmed them.
